name: ATP charge against adenylylated dead-end formation
scale_system: bench, 1 mM substrate, six chemically modified fragments assembling a 22/23-mer GalNAc siRNA with a T4 RNA ligase 2 fused to a polyphosphate kinase; the opposing bound is from unmodified DNA on RNA splints, so the mechanism transfers and the number does not
notes: THE MODEL ROW, AND IT IS REWRITTEN RATHER THAN DELETED. More blocks means more junctions means more ATP; but abortive adenylylation, which produces the unfilterable AppN dead end, is suppressed by LESS ATP. So the two parameters are genuinely opposed and the opposition is real. WHAT IS NOT TRUE, AND WAS PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN, IS THAT THE WINDOW IS EMPTY. The 'at least 4 mM ATP' sentence is verbatim in SRC-WO2025262452 and appears twice, but read in place it is the STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM THAT DOCUMENT'S INVENTION SOLVES: it is immediately followed by the observation that no product forms when AMP is supplied instead, and that activity 'can be rescued by the addition of PPK and polyphosphate'. The same document then teaches the opposite operating condition - 'less than about 4 mM ATP and/or AMP, optionally ... 0.5 mM or less' (four occurrences), 'the ATP regeneration system overcomes the requirement for high concentrations of ATP', and 'complete ligation ... in the presence of sub-stoichiometric quantities of ATP or AMP'. The suppression side is softer than claimed too: SRC-PBCV1-2014 reports little inhibition at 1 mM ATP for most sequences, not a hard ceiling at 100 uM. SO THE CORNER IS MARKED unknown RATHER THAN unreachable, and no claim of a window empty by 6-40x is written anywhere. The mechanism that reconciles the two bounds - in-situ regeneration from AMP plus polyphosphate - is exemplified in the very document cited for the high bound, which also means the earlier claim that fed-batch has no demonstration anywhere is wrong: ATP-limited feeding and in-situ generation are mechanistically the same move, and one of them IS exemplified. Regeneration carries its own ceiling, verbatim 'a maximum of 66 % conversion to ATP'. See Q-040, R-010, IMP-APPN.

name: ATP charge draws down free magnesium
scale_system: the divalent-cation range quoted is CLAIM language from a bench patent ('5-100 mM, optionally 30-50 mM'), not a measured specification; the 1:1 ATP-magnesium chelation stoichiometry is general solution chemistry, and the activity threshold it is set against was measured on unmodified DNA
notes: A COUPLING NOBODY HAD REGISTERED, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT REACHES DOWNSTREAM. ATP chelates magnesium roughly one for one, so in a 10 mM MgCl2 buffer (BUF-LIG) a high ATP charge leaves little free Mg2+ - and the ligase needs free Mg2+, not total. That is why SRC-WO2025262452 ties the two together explicitly, verbatim: 'The divalent cation concentration will typically depend on the amount of ATP required.' The corner is marked UNREACHABLE on arithmetic rather than on a measurement: a high segment concentration demands proportionally more ATP (four junctions per strand), and at 10 mM total magnesium the free fraction cannot supply both. THE REASON IT MATTERS IS NOT THE REACTION, IT IS THE PLANT. Raising magnesium to compensate - which the cited claim language contemplates at up to 100 mM - loads exactly the species the register says does not diafilter: magnesium binds the polyanion and resists buffer exchange (R-014, IMP-DIVALENT, SRC-GRONKE-2023). So the buffer envelope propagates into diafiltration load and waste volume. One consequence points the other way and is worth keeping: chelating at the quench converts free Mg2+ into the net-negative Mg-EDTA complex, which should pass a membrane that the free cation does not (inference, C-014, Q-059). Because this corner is declared unreachable, no design_intent band on either parameter may span to include it - and neither carries one today, so the rule is proven by mutation rather than by a live row, the same standing as not_measurable in gen/controls.py.

name: Concentration against specific reaction rate (substrate inhibition)
scale_system: NO SOURCE KEY IS CARRIED: the rate law behind this coupling was fitted over 30 nM to 20 uM on 12-bp modified RNA fragments with a DIFFERENT enzyme, and its document could not be retrieved this session, so no constant from it is registered anywhere
notes: THE MECHANISM THAT EXPLAINS THE VOID IN ENV-006, carried as a mechanism and explicitly NOT as numbers. Ligases show substrate inhibition, so specific rate rises with concentration, peaks, and then falls. The consequence for a plant is the one that matters and it is qualitative: raising concentration buys volumetric loading and pays it back in rate, so CONCENTRATING THE LIGATION MAY NOT SHRINK THE PLANT AT ALL. That is a prediction of exactly what SRC-ALMAC-2023 observed qualitatively at 10 mM - 'slow and failed to go completion'. The corner 'high concentration with short hold time' is therefore declared unreachable. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: no inhibition constant, no kcat and no Km appears in any register row, because the only retrieved figures sit just ABOVE the top of their own fitted range (an extrapolation) on an enzyme that is not a candidate here, and the document was not retrievable for verification. Registering the mechanism without the numbers is the honest position and it is Q-066. Note this coupling also explains why the 10 mM endpoint of ENV-006 is a failure rather than a limit - the reaction does not stop, it slows.

name: Reaction temperature is bounded by the enzyme, not by the duplex
scale_system: every retrieved ligation temperature is 30 C or below, across bench patents on modified and phosphodiester substrates alike; the enzyme stability figure that would set the ceiling is NOT registered because its document could not be retrieved
notes: THIS ROW EXISTS TO RECORD THAT TWO PARAMETERS WERE WRONGLY COUPLED. R-003, C-004 and P-LIG-T all imply the duplex melting band bounds the reaction temperature from above. It does not: every retrieved ligation runs at 30 C or below, 28 C or more below the bottom of the melting band, so the duplex is nowhere near binding. The real ceiling is ENZYME stability, and it is far lower. The corner 'reaction temperature high AND duplex intact' is unreachable not because the duplex fails but because THE ENZYME FAILS FIRST, which is a different and more restrictive constraint than the one the register carried. Evidence that the enzyme is the binding limit is direct: in SRC-USPTO-10640812 the Chlorella virus ligase gave verbatim 'At 25 C. ... no full length product was observed. At 30 C. and 37 C., full length product was detected' - activity rising with temperature over a range entirely below the duplex band - while in SRC-NEB-WO2023173098 soluble T4 DNA ligase 'showed no or residual ligase activity after treatment at 45 C for 30 min'. NO NUMERIC ENZYME CEILING IS WRITTEN: the two figures that circulated are midpoints of residual-activity curves after a 60-minute hold, not melting temperatures, and their document could not be retrieved, so comparing them with P-DS-TM as like-for-like would be a category error on top of an unverifiable number (Q-059).

name: Inactivation temperature against duplex integrity
scale_system: bench batch ligations; the inactivation band is from four documents on three enzyme forms, the melting band from two rows of one table on a duplex with only THREE modified positions - so neither side of this coupling is measured on our material
notes: THE COUPLING BEHIND R-021, STATED AS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN AS A WORRY: the whole of the documented inactivation band (ENV-005, 80-95 C) sits above the whole of the measured melting band (ENV-010, 58.1-64.1 C), so there is NO overlap in which the enzyme is killed by heat and the duplex is left below its melting point. The corner 'inactivation at the low end AND duplex well within its melting band' is unreachable, and it would stay unreachable even at the bottom of the inactivation band. THE MECHANISM MATTERS FOR THE MITIGATION AND IT WAS PREVIOUSLY WRONG: melting is reversible, so crossing the melting point is not itself the damage; the irreversible hazard is Mg2+-assisted hydrolysis and depurination sustained THROUGH the hold, with the divalent cation still present at 10 mM in the demonstrated buffer. Read that way the mitigation is chelation rather than a lower setpoint, which is why C-014 points at EDTA. And the escape route of inactivating while the material is single-stranded is unavailable for the LIGASE - the splint IS the complementary product strand, so the product is duplex from the first ligation onward - while being exactly what the demonstrated route does for the KINASE at 75 C before annealing.

name: Vessel scale against anneal ramp time
scale_system: FIRST PRINCIPLES, ours, with no source: geometric similarity gives specific heat-transfer area falling as the cube root of volume. The 15 min anneal it is applied to is measured at bench scale (SRC-ALMAC-2023); nothing measures it at 1 L, let alone above
notes: A COUPLING BETWEEN A PROCESS TIME AND A FACILITY DECISION, and the one that turns a bench condition into an equipment fork. For geometrically similar vessels the jacket area per unit volume falls as the cube root of the volume, so going from 1 L to 1000 L loses exactly 10x in specific area: a 15 minute ramp to 65 C becomes of order 150 minutes at the same jacket temperature difference. The corner 'short anneal AND large batch' is therefore unreachable in a jacketed vessel, and the alternatives are a higher jacket temperature, which the enzyme ceiling forbids (CPL-004), or moving the anneal out of the reactor into a higher-area device, which is an unregistered equipment fork (Q-065). NOTE THE DIRECTION OF THE COUPLING WITH CONCENTRATION, because it is the opposite of intuition: a LOWER titre needs a LARGER vessel for the same batch mass, so the ramp problem is worst exactly where ENV-006's void leaves us - unable to demonstrate a higher concentration. This is why P-CONC-LIG being an upper BOUND rather than a titre matters for the facility and not only for the balance.
